The version that survives contact with data measures the move in price. A candle is a bullish order block if it closes down, price trades some distance above its high within the next few bars, and it is the last down candle before that move — where two or more consecutive down candles would qualify off the same move, only the last is marked, which is what the word last in the definition is doing. A bearish one mirrors. Now the threshold is out in the open: some distance, and a few bars. Set the distance as a multiple of the average bar range and the window at three bars, and the rule is complete. Two numbers, both yours, and the rest is mechanical.
